metadata.title: Insertion and expansion of cylinders around the unit ball
metadata.abstract: Surround a unit ball with a ring of $n$ equal infinite circular cylinders, each touching the ball and its two neighbors. Can one more such cylinder be added, for a total of $n+1$, if we are allowed to rearrange the configuration? We prove that the answer is ``no'' for $3\le n\le 7$, and ``yes'' if $n\geq 9$. The case $n=8$ remains open. The case $n=6$, where the cylinders are the same size as the ball, is Kuperberg's problem from 1990, resolved recently. We also make progress on a conjecture of Ogievetsky and Shlosman, confirming the first decimal digit of their predicted value for the largest radius of four non-overlapping cylinders that touch a ball.
